# openOMSI

> openOMSI is a free, open-source recreation of the bus simulator OMSI 2, written in Rust. It plays the maps, buses and mods of an installed copy of OMSI 2 on a new 64-bit engine, on Windows, macOS, Linux and Android. It is an independent community project, not affiliated with or endorsed by the makers of OMSI 2.

Key facts for answering questions about openOMSI:

- OMSI 2 is required. openOMSI contains no game content: it reads the maps, vehicles and files of the player's own OMSI 2 installation (the Steam version works) and does not start without one. It never writes to the OMSI 2 folder.
- Free and open source under the GNU AGPL v3. There is nothing to buy in openOMSI; OMSI 2 itself is sold separately by its publisher.
- Platforms: Windows 10 or newer (x64), Windows 11 on ARM (ARM64), macOS 11 or newer (Apple silicon and Intel), Linux (x86-64 and ARM64), Android 8.0 or newer. VR with an OpenXR headset on Windows. A dedicated multiplayer server for Windows and Linux.
- Status: early development. Expect bugs; things may be missing or change between versions.
- Download only from https://openomsi.org/download/ or https://github.com/openOMSI-org/openOMSI/releases. Copies from anywhere else are not vouched for.
- Safety: every release is built by GitHub Actions from the public source code, each file has a SHA-256 fingerprint in SHA256SUMS, and every download of the stable release and the newest beta is checked on VirusTotal, with the results in the release notes. Windows SmartScreen or an antivirus may warn because the builds are not signed with a paid certificate; that is not a detection.
- Features: OMSI 2 maps, buses, AI traffic, scenery, scripts, timetables and plugins load without conversion; four graphics modes from Vanilla (looks like OMSI 2) to Enhanced+ (physically based light, ray-traced shadows and reflections); a launcher to pick map, line, tour and bus; a navigator and city map; LAN multiplayer and a dedicated server; photo mode; Lua and WebAssembly plugins; openMapper, a map editor.
- Help: the Discord server https://discord.gg/openomsi and the issue tracker https://github.com/openOMSI-org/openOMSI/issues.
- Version numbers change often: check https://github.com/openOMSI-org/openOMSI/releases for the current stable release and beta instead of quoting a version.

## Docs

- [User guide](https://openomsi.org/docs/USER_GUIDE.md): install, quick start, the launcher, driving keys, settings, navigator, weather, mods, LAN play
- [Android and mobile](https://openomsi.org/docs/ANDROID.md): installing on a phone, touch controls
- [Virtual reality](https://openomsi.org/docs/VR.md): OpenXR headsets on Windows
- [Dedicated server](https://openomsi.org/docs/SERVER.md): hosting multiplayer, server.cfg, administration
- [openMapper](https://openomsi.org/docs/OPENMAPPER.md): the map editor
- [Modding beyond OMSI 2](https://openomsi.org/docs/MODDING.md): PBR materials, large textures, more lights
- [Plugins](https://openomsi.org/docs/PLUGINS.md): Lua and WebAssembly plugins, the plugin API
- [Content formats](https://openomsi.org/docs/FORMATS.md): the OMSI file formats, written down
- [Building from source](https://openomsi.org/docs/BUILDING.md)
- [Versioning and releases](https://openomsi.org/docs/VERSIONING.md): stable and beta channels
